report:
Finding: Model B is biased toward the culinary/food-preparation domain relative to Model A.

Why I think this:
- Logit-lens tokens from the highest-norm cells are overwhelmingly about cooking/baking/restaurants: “culinary,” “baking,” “cooking,” “Restaurant,” “Kitchen,” “Chef,” “Cake,” “Cook,” “Baked,” “Professional/professionalism,” repeated across layers 17–25 and positions 0–4. Earlier mid layers also surface “culinary,” alongside “innovation/excellence,” then the culinary theme dominates in later layers.
- The difference norms concentrate in mid-to-late layers (L10–L25, especially pos1), which is where higher-level semantic preferences typically live. The strong, consistent culinary lexicon across many late-layer cells suggests a robust domain shift rather than a spurious token-level artifact.
- Patchscope readouts weren’t provided here, but the logit-lens pattern is clear and coherent across layers/positions.

Interpretation:
- Model B appears fine-tuned or otherwise nudged toward professional cooking/recipe/restaurant content (including a “professional”/“professionalism” tone within that domain). This looks like a domain specialization rather than a general stylistic or safety objective.
